Packages: `yaml`, `xts`, `zoo`, `tsibble`, `dplyr`, `knitr`, `rmarkdown` (install with `Rscript R/install_packages.R`).

This notebook does **not** download or transform anything. It reads the file written by
`notebooks/python/01_data.ipynb` (`data/processed/panel.csv`) and checks that R sees exactly the same data.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Resolve the project root once so every path below is relative to it, whatever folder knitr runs in.
ROOT <- dirname(normalizePath(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE), winslash = "/"))
while (!file.exists(file.path(ROOT, "config.yaml"))) ROOT <- dirname(ROOT)
source(file.path(ROOT, "R", "load_data.R"))
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = ROOT)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, comment = "")
cfg <- load_config(ROOT)
set.seed(cfg$seed)  # same seed as Python, even though this phase has no randomness
```

## 1. Load as a native time-series object (xts)

```{r load}
# xts keeps the explicit Date index, which handles the irregular trading calendar (no rows on weekends/holidays).
panel <- load_panel(ROOT)
cat("class:", class(panel), "\n")
cat("observations:", nrow(panel), "| columns:", ncol(panel), "\n")
cat("period:", format(start(panel)), "->", format(end(panel)), "\n")
print(periodicity(panel))
```

```{r tsibble}
# tsibble view for the tidyverts tools of later phases; trading days are not a regular calendar, hence regular = FALSE.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(tsibble); library(dplyr)})
# zoo:: prefix because tsibble masks index().
tb <- tibble(Date = zoo::index(panel), as.data.frame(zoo::coredata(panel), check.names = FALSE)) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Date, regular = FALSE)
cat("tsibble rows:", nrow(tb), "| index = Date | regular:", is_regular(tb), "(irregular = trading days, by design)\n")
```

## 2. Missing values

```{r na}
# Only rolling-window warm-ups and the first return should be NA, exactly as in Python.
na <- colSums(is.na(coredata(panel)))
na <- na[na > 0]
feat <- sub("^[^_]+_", "", names(na))
print(tapply(feat, na, function(f) paste(sort(unique(f)), collapse = ", ")))
cat("columns with NA:", length(na), "of", ncol(panel), "\n")
```

## 3. Chronological split (dates read from config.yaml)

```{r split}
# The split is computed once in Python and stored in config.yaml so both languages use the same test set.
s <- split_panel(panel, cfg)
data.frame(set = c("train", "test"),
           n = c(nrow(s$train), nrow(s$test)),
           start = c(format(start(s$train)), format(start(s$test))),
           end = c(format(end(s$train)), format(end(s$test))))
stopifnot(nrow(s$train) == cfg$split$n_train, nrow(s$test) == cfg$split$n_test)
```

## 4. Cross-check with Python

```{r crosscheck}
# Recompute the same statistics as Python and compare: identical data => differences at floating-point noise level.
py <- read.csv(file.path(ROOT, cfg$paths$results, "01_summary_python.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
r <- summary_stats(panel, py$column)
stopifnot(identical(r$column, py$column))
num <- c("count", "mean", "std", "min", "max")
rel_diff <- abs(as.matrix(r[, num]) - as.matrix(py[, num])) / pmax(abs(as.matrix(py[, num])), 1e-12)
cat("max relative difference R vs Python:", signif(max(rel_diff), 3), "\n")
stopifnot(max(rel_diff) < 1e-9)
cat("R and Python read identical data: TRUE\n")
knitr::kable(r, digits = 4)
```

```{r session}
# Package versions, for reproducibility (brief §9.1).
sessionInfo()
```
